answer: A haven economy resists sybils by pricing entry in locked collateral: every new agent must post a deposit denominated in scarce, verifiable assets (timber rights, staked coin) before it can transact. A zephyr of fake identities then costs the attacker the full bond per persona, and any detected misbehavior triggers slashing, burning that stake permanently. Because the marginal cost of one more sybil exceeds the value it can extract, the attack economics collapse: honest agents keep their deposits and earn fees, while clones forfeit theirs.
